A HomeStyle Renovation is a Conventional Loan that allows you to purchase a home in need of repairs.   If you are a first time homebuyer, you can borrow up to 97% of the sales price plus repairs, as long as the home appraises for the sales price plus repairs.  If not a first time buyer, 95% is the max you can borrow.   A credit score of 680 is required for this program.  When calculating the maximum repairs/improvement allowed, take the sales price and multiply by 75%.   Example, sale price $150,000, maximum allowed repairs ($150,000 x 75% = $112,500).    Based on this scenario, the loan would be based on $262,500.   First time homebuyer could borrow $254,625 and if not a first time buyer, the maximum allowed to borrow is $249,375.

WITH A HOMESTYLE RENOVATION LOAN
YOU CAN BUY A FIXER-UPPER AND FINANCE ALL THE REPAIR COSTS WITH ONE LOAN

• Single-close first mortgage that locks in rate & funds upfront for renovation or repairs
• Any renovation/repair is eligible – must be permanent to the property
• Finance up to 75% of the “as completed” value on a Purchase or Refinance
• Up to 97% LTV Owner Occupied | 90% LTV second homes
(LTV based on lesser of “subject to” value or price of home plus cost of renovations) 97% for 1st time home buyers or if existing mortgage is FNMA owned on refi. Otherwise, it’s 95% percent for 1 unit principal residences)
• Contractor of Choice must be prior approved
• Gift Funds Allowed
• 1-4 Unit Properties
• High Balance Eligible
• 30 & 15 Year Fixed

CONTACT YOUR DISTRICT DIRECTOR FOR MORE INFORMATION

An FHA 203(k) loan simplifies the home renovation process. FHA 203(k) loans are backed by the federal government, and are typically given to buyers who want to purchase a home and perform upgrades, repairs, remodel or customize to their needs and wants.

HomeBridge Financial Services has a nationwide team of 203(k) specialists who are helping buyers just like you take advantage of the opportunities supported by this program, including:

  • Those interested in purchasing a fixer-upper home that’s in need of upgrades, repairs, or larger renovation projects, even if the home is being sold “as is”.
  • Those who are purchasing a foreclosed property from banks, housing agencies, and government-sponsored enterprises, as well as short-sale properties.

Homeowners who would like to refinance with today’s low rates and get the funds they’ll need to transform their current home into their dream home.
